data.title: Keloid and hypertrophic scar — viva
data.summary: Benign tumours & cysts · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Keloid and hypertrophic scar** (Benign tumours & cysts)_

**Q1. Define and differentiate keloid and hypertrophic scar.**
- Both are abnormal fibroproliferative wound healing with excess collagen
- Hypertrophic scar: raised scar confined to the original wound, appears within weeks, may regress over 1–2 years, common across tension lines/joints (burns), no racial predilection, lower recurrence after excision
- Keloid: extends beyond original wound margins (claw-like), appears months–years after injury (or spontaneously), does not regress, recurs after excision, more in dark skin (Africans, Asians), familial, sites — sternum, shoulders, upper back, earlobes (piercing), mandible; itchy and painful

**Q2. Pathogenesis.**
- Prolonged inflammation and fibroblast hyperactivity: increased TGF-β1/β2 (decreased TGF-β3), PDGF, VEGF, IL-6; excess type I collagen (keloid) / type III (hypertrophic early); reduced apoptosis, mechanical tension, hypoxia
- Genetic: HLA associations, NEDD4, familial AD forms; hormones (puberty, pregnancy enlarge)

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Keloid: thick, hyalinised, eosinophilic glassy collagen bundles ('keloidal collagen') haphazardly arranged, fewer fibroblasts, mucin, no nodules
- Hypertrophic scar: nodules of fine collagen and myofibroblasts (α-SMA+) arranged parallel to the surface, more vessels

**Q4. Assessment.**
- Vancouver Scar Scale (vascularity, pigmentation, pliability, height), POSAS (Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale)

**Q5. Prevention.**
- Avoid elective surgery/piercing/tattoos in keloid-prone individuals; minimal tension closure along relaxed skin tension lines; early silicone gel/sheets and pressure garments after surgery/burns; prompt treatment of acne

**Q6. Discuss treatment (combination approach).**
- First line: intralesional triamcinolone acetonide 10–40 mg/ml every 3–4 weeks (side effects — atrophy, hypopigmentation, telangiectasia), silicone gel/sheets (12–24 h/day for months), pressure therapy (earlobe pressure earrings, garments 24–30 mmHg)
- Combined: intralesional 5-FU (with steroid), bleomycin, verapamil; cryotherapy (contact or intralesional cryoprobe) before steroid; botulinum toxin A
- Surgery: excision (intramarginal/core excision) ALWAYS followed by adjuvant therapy (steroids, pressure, radiation) — excision alone has 50–100% recurrence
- Radiotherapy: postoperative superficial X-ray or electron beam/brachytherapy within 24–72 h (recurrent/large keloids in adults)
- Lasers: pulsed-dye laser (erythema, itch), fractional CO2 laser with laser-assisted drug delivery
- Others: imiquimod post-excision, topical/oral tranilast, dupilumab (reports), fat grafting/PRP (hypertrophic)

**Q7. Discuss relaxed skin tension lines (PYQ).**
- Lines of minimal tension on relaxed skin, perpendicular to underlying muscle pull (follow wrinkles on face — Borges' lines); incisions parallel to RSTL heal with narrow, less noticeable scars and less hypertrophy, vs Langer's lines (cleavage lines on cadavers)

**Q8. Which sites are keloid-prone and why?**
- Presternal, shoulders/deltoid, upper back, ear lobes (piercing), mandibular area — high skin tension and movement (presternal, shoulder) and sebaceous-rich areas; genetics (darker skin, family history, HLA), pregnancy and puberty (hormonal) increase risk

**Q9. Intralesional steroid technique.**
- Triamcinolone acetonide 10–40 mg/ml injected into the upper/mid dermis of the keloid (blanching), using 26–30 G needle or dermojet, every 3–6 weeks; can combine with 5-FU (50 mg/ml, 9:1 or 3:1 ratio), cryotherapy before injection softens lesion; side effects — atrophy, hypopigmentation, telangiectasia, Cushingoid if large doses

**Q10. What are the newer treatments?**
- Intralesional verapamil, bleomycin, botulinum toxin A, PRP; pulsed-dye laser for erythema, fractional CO2 with drug delivery, intralesional cryotherapy (cryoneedle), postoperative radiotherapy (electron beam within 24–48 h), silicone gel/sheet for ≥12 h/day for 3 months, pressure earrings after ear keloid excision, dupilumab (case reports)

## Quick spotter facts
- Scar extending beyond wound margins, not regressing, on the sternum/earlobe — keloid
- Excision only with adjuvant (steroid/radiation/pressure)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Keloids and hypertrophic scars); International scar management recommendations. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
